subject.title: exec auto-reviewer re-bills a fresh model completion for every byte-identical repeated exec

question: May the model-backed exec reviewer reuse cached decisions for byte-identical exec review inputs, and should that cache be per reviewer/run keyed by the full reviewed input or prompt?
rationale: The source bug is clear, but exec review caching changes when OpenClaw asks the model again before allowing an approval miss, so cache lifetime and key scope need explicit approval-boundary intent.

options.title: Approve full-input per-run memo
options.body: Cache parsed reviewer decisions only inside the shared reviewer instance, keyed by the full reviewed input or prompt, without persisting or converting them to durable approvals.

options.title: Memoize allow-once only
options.body: Cache only low-risk allow-once results and keep ask, timeout, and error decisions uncached for a narrower behavior change with smaller savings.

options.title: Keep fresh review semantics
options.body: Accept the repeated model cost to preserve one-request-one-review semantics until stronger security or live billing evidence is available.

recommendation.title: Approve full-input per-run memo
recommendation.body: Cache parsed reviewer decisions only inside the shared reviewer instance, keyed by the full reviewed input or prompt, without persisting or converting them to durable approvals.

likelyOwner.reason: jesse-merhi is the strongest available owner signal for normalized exec auto-review and adjacent approval-boundary work.
